audits.mathematicalReason: The square has side length 1 inch. Right triangles DCM and BCN have equal hypotenuses CM=CN and equal legs DC=BC, so HL gives DM=BN. Hence AM=AN=t, where 0<t<1. Equilateral side equality and Pythagoras give MN²=2t²=CM²=1+(1−t)². Thus (t+1)²=3, and the admissible root is t=√3−1. Subtracting the three corner triangles from the square gives [CMN]=1−t²/2−(1−t)=2√3−3. This supports the equilateral-triangle and triangle-area assessments and the listed congruence and composite-area support. The alternative route is also valid: the equal angles DCM and BCN total 30°, so each is 15°, and DM=tan(45°−30°)=2−√3.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let E be the second circle intersection on the ray from B through C and D. Tangent-secant power gives 6²=BC·BE=3BE, so BE=12. Since BD=6, DE=6. At the interior point D, the positive chord product is DC·DE=r²−OD², so 18=r²−4 and r=√22. The radius is the positive root. The alternate route is independently valid: C is the midpoint of DB, OC=r, and tangent-radius perpendicularity gives OB²=r²+36. The median identity in triangle ODB gives 4r²=2OD²+2OB²−DB²=2r²+44, again yielding r²=22. Power of a point is therefore a defensible assessed node for the product route, not a requirement of the alternate route.

audits.mathematicalReason: Because M is the midpoint of BC and G lies on AM, triangles ABG and ACG have equal areas. Therefore [AFG]/[AEG]=(AF/AB)/(AE/AC)=(AF/12)/(2AF/16)=2/3. Triangles AFG and AEG share the same altitude to line EF, so GF/GE=2/3 and EG/GF=3/2. This directly supports proportional-segment manipulation, with median and triangle-area facts supplying one valid route. The similarity route is also defensible: draw the parallel to BC through E, meeting AB at H and AM at K. Similarity gives AH=3AF/2 and HK=KE. A second parallel through F, meeting AM at J, gives FJ/EK=2/3; similarity of triangles FJG and EKG then yields GF/GE=2/3.

audits.mathematicalReason: For a>0, the sublevel set 2Max(|x|,|y|)≤a is the axis-aligned square with vertices (±a/2,±a/2). The sublevel set √(2(x²+y²))≤a is the disk x²+y²≤a²/2, whose radius is a/√2. Finally, |x|+|y|≤a is the diamond with vertices (±a,0) and (0,±a). The specified reversal of inequality into sublevel-set containment therefore requires an axis-aligned square inside a circle inside a diamond, exactly figure II. At a=0 all three sets are the origin, and for a<0 all are empty. The candidate scopes appropriately cover containment, coordinate descriptions of the squares, and recognition of the circle equation; proving the displayed inequalities by a separate inequality theorem is not necessary.

audits.mathematicalReason: Write α=∠BAC and β=∠ABC. Since O is the incenter, AD bisects angle A and BO bisects angle B. The inscribed-angle theorem gives ∠CBD=∠CAD=α/2 and ∠BCD=∠BAD=α/2, so BD=CD. No equality with the circumradius is needed.

audits.mathematicalReason: Use inches and place the hole center at (0,0), with radius 3/2. In the displayed configuration, the radius-1 plug has center (0,−1/2), and the radius-1/2 plug has center (0,1). If a new gauge has radius r and center (x,y), tangency gives x²+y²=(3/2−r)², x²+(y+1/2)²=(1+r)², and x²+(y−1)²=(1/2+r)². The first equation represents internal tangency; the other two represent external tangency. Subtracting the first equation from the others gives y=5r−3/2 and y=3/2−2r. Thus r=3/7, so d=6/7≈0.85714, rounding to 0.86 inches. The centers (±6/7,9/14) realize the two symmetric gauges. Circle-position relations, Pythagoras, elimination, and rounding all fit the proposed scopes.

audits.mathematicalReason: Take A=(0,0), B=(w,0), C=(w,h), D=(0,h), and P=(x,y). Pythagoras gives PA²=x²+y², PC²=(w−x)²+(h−y)², PD²=x²+(h−y)², and PB²=(w−x)²+y². Therefore PA²+PC²=PD²+PB², since the perpendicular-component terms match. Substituting the given distances gives PB²=3²+5²−4²=18, hence PB=3√2 inches. This establishes the relation directly from Pythagoras and rectangle properties, so no additional theorem node is necessary.
